My sorghum plot is small, only about a quarter of my land, and I am intercropping it as we always do here in Benshangul-Gumuz to spread the risk. I cannot afford much chemical fertilizer — the price is high and the shops are far — but I will try to put a little DAP at planting if I can get it on credit from the cooperative, and I will spread the manure from my animals on this plot because it is close to the homestead. I will use my own sorghum seed saved from last year since the improved varieties are not easy to find and I trust the local one for our rains. The rains should be enough, so no irrigation, and weeding will be done by me, my wife, and the older children with hand hoes; I may call two neighbors for a few days at weeding time and pay them with food and a little cash.
